metadata.title: Cross-Lingual Social Fatigue on Mastodon: 63,797 LLM-Verified Fatigue Expressions and Annotation Pipeline
metadata.description:
Companion data and code release for the Information Processing & Management paper "Understanding Cross-Lingual Social Fatigue in Decentralized Social Media: An LLM-Enhanced Computational Analysis of 26 Million Mastodon Posts."

This deposit contains per-post fatigue labels for 63,797 verified fatigue expressions, drawn from a 26.3-million-post multilingual Mastodon corpus (FediLive archive). Each record carries a stable post URI, language, linguistic group, a semicolon-joined set of five dimensional labels (physical_fatigue, mental_cognitive_fatigue, emotional_fatigue, digital_social_fatigue, existential_resignation), and a per-dimension confidence score (0 = absent). Labels were produced by a zero-shot verification pass with Qwen3-8B-Instruct; a second annotator (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) was used in the accompanying sensitivity analysis.

Also included: the fatigue keyword taxonomies used for candidate retrieval -- an English taxonomy (fatigue_taxonomy.json) and an expanded multilingual taxonomy covering Japanese, German, French, Spanish, Dutch, and Portuguese (fatigue_taxonomy_multilingual.json), together with their source -- the English and non-English verification prompts and user-message template, and the analysis code that reproduces every result in the paper (lexicon retrieval, BERT re-ranking, full-corpus labeling, robustness/AN-01 and AN-02 sensitivity analyses, and the release-building script).

Ethical note: raw post text is intentionally NOT redistributed, to respect Fediverse community norms and minimize re-identification risk. Each record carries only a stable post URI from which the original public post can be re-derived via the FediLive archive; no personally identifying information is included. Because the study uses only publicly accessible, non-identifiable social-media content and involves no interaction with or intervention on users, it does not constitute human-subjects research and was exempt from IRB approval.
references: Min, H., et al. (2025). FediLive: A live-feed archive of the Fediverse. [Corresponding citation to be inserted once published.]
metadata.notes: Top-level license is CC-BY-4.0 (data, lexicon, prompts). The analysis code in code/ is released under the MIT License (see LICENSE). Raw post text is excluded; post URIs permit re-derivation from the public FediLive archive.
metadata.method: Fatigue candidates were retrieved with a multilingual keyword lexicon, optionally re-ranked with multilingual sentence-transformer embeddings (BERT re-ranking), and verified zero-shot with Qwen3-8B-Instruct at temperature 0.1. Per-post records report a 5-dimension label set and confidence weights. A second LLM annotator (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) provided independent labels for annotator-sensitivity analysis.
